question_defect: Printed option 4 is written ₁₅Si³¹, pairing atomic number 15 with the symbol Si; silicon has atomic number 14, so this distractor contradicts itself. It does not affect which option is correct.
notes: Solved independently before reading the solution: conserving charge gives Z(X) = 13 + 2 − 0 = 15 and conserving mass number gives A(X) = 27 + 4 − 1 = 30, and element 15 is phosphorus, so X is ₁₅P³⁰, printed option 3. Every step line follows from the one above it and the why_this_step is a true statement of the conservation used. Both common_mistakes routes were recomputed and reach the options they name: omitting the neutron's mass number gives A = 31 with Z = 15, printed option 1, and treating the neutron as carrying charge +1 gives Z = 13 + 2 − 1 = 14 with A = 30, which is silicon-30, printed option 2. Both are genuine bookkeeping slips here and neither condemns a correct method. difficulty easy is right; mistake_type_hint calculation is defensible since both listed errors are arithmetic in the conservation ledger rather than a misunderstanding of the principle, so it was not filed.
